source.verification: All type/category names, allowed mappings and sane defaults match the live API; descriptions come from the same checked-out model.

md5.formdesc: You are encouraged to use filename|md5 instead. A checksum in md5 format, only use this if you don't know the correct filename

sha1.formdesc: You are encouraged to use filename|sha1 instead. A checksum in sha1 format, only use this if you don't know the correct filename

sha256.formdesc: You are encouraged to use filename|sha256 instead. A checksum in sha256 format, only use this if you don't know the correct filename

filename|md5.desc: A filename and an MD5 hash separated by a |
filename|md5.formdesc: A filename and an md5 hash separated by a | (no spaces)

filename|sha1.desc: A filename and an SHA1 hash separated by a |
filename|sha1.formdesc: A filename and a sha1 hash separated by a | (no spaces)

filename|sha256.desc: A filename and an SHA256 hash separated by a |
filename|sha256.formdesc: A filename and a sha256 hash separated by a | (no spaces)

ip-src.desc: A source IP address of the attacker

ip-dst.desc: A destination IP address of the attacker or C&C server
ip-dst.formdesc: A destination IP address of the attacker or C&C server. Also set the IDS flag on when this IP is hardcoded in malware

hostname.desc: A full host/dnsname of an attacker
hostname.formdesc: A full host/dnsname of an attacker. Also set the IDS flag on when this hostname is hardcoded in malware

domain.desc: A domain name used in the malware
domain.formdesc: A domain name used in the malware. Use this instead of hostname when the upper domain is important or can be used to create links between events.

domain|ip.desc: A domain name and its IP address (as found in DNS lookup) separated by a |
domain|ip.formdesc: A domain name and its IP address (as found in DNS lookup) separated by a | (no spaces)

email-src.desc: The source email address. Used to describe the sender when describing an e-mail.

eppn.desc: eduPersonPrincipalName - eppn - the NetId of the person for the purposes of inter-institutional authentication. Should be stored in the form of user@univ.edu, where univ.edu is the name of the local security domain.

email-dst.desc: The destination email address. Used to describe the recipient when describing an e-mail.

email-attachment.desc: File name of the email attachment.

http-method.desc: HTTP method used by the malware (e.g. POST, GET, ...).

user-agent.desc: The user-agent used by the malware in the HTTP request.

ja3-fingerprint-md5.desc: JA3 is a method for creating SSL/TLS client fingerprints that should be easy to produce on any platform and can be easily shared for threat intelligence.

jarm-fingerprint.desc: JARM is a method for creating SSL/TLS server fingerprints.

favicon-mmh3.desc: favicon-mmh3 is the murmur3 hash of a favicon as used in Shodan.

hassh-md5.desc: hassh is a network fingerprinting standard which can be used to identify specific Client SSH implementations. The fingerprints can be easily stored, searched and shared in the form of an MD5 fingerprint.

hasshserver-md5.desc: hasshServer is a network fingerprinting standard which can be used to identify specific Server SSH implementations. The fingerprints can be easily stored, searched and shared in the form of an MD5 fingerprint.

snort.desc: An IDS rule in Snort rule-format
snort.formdesc: An IDS rule in Snort rule-format. This rule will be automatically rewritten in the NIDS exports.

suricata.desc: An IDS rule in Suricata rule-format
suricata.formdesc: An IDS rule in Suricata rule-format. This rule will be automatically rewritten in the NIDS exports.

bro.desc: An NIDS rule in the Bro rule-format
bro.formdesc: An NIDS rule in the Bro rule-format.

zeek.desc: An NIDS rule in the Zeek rule-format
zeek.formdesc: An NIDS rule in the Zeek rule-format.

community-id.desc: A community ID flow hashing algorithm to map multiple traffic monitors into common flow id
community-id.formdesc: a community ID flow hashing algorithm to map multiple traffic monitors into common flow id

dom-hash.desc: A dom-hash algorithm is a structural fingerprint of an HTML Document Object Model where all tag names are contained in a single string separated by a pipe. The truncated SHA252 value by the first 32-character serves as fingerprint.
dom-hash.formdesc: A dom-hash value is a structural fingerprint to uniquely identify an HTML Document Object Model.

pattern-in-file.desc: Pattern in file that identifies the malware

pattern-in-traffic.desc: Pattern in network traffic that identifies the malware

pattern-in-memory.desc: Pattern in memory dump that identifies the malware

filename-pattern.desc: A pattern in the name of a file

ssh-fingerprint.desc: A fingerprint of SSH key material

sigma.desc: Sigma - Generic Signature Format for SIEM Systems

kusto-query.desc: Kusto query - Kusto from Microsoft Azure is a service for storing and running interactive analytics over Big Data.

mime-type.desc: A media type (also MIME type and content type) is a two-part identifier for file formats and format contents transmitted on the Internet

cookie.desc: HTTP cookie as often stored on the user web client. This can include authentication cookie or session cookie.

vulnerability.desc: A reference to the vulnerability (examples: GCVE id, CVE id, GHSA id, etc)

cpe.desc: Common Platform Enumeration - structured naming scheme for information technology systems, software, and packages.

weakness.desc: A reference to the weakness (CWE) used in the exploit

attachment.formdesc: Please upload files using the Upload Attachment button.

malware-sample.formdesc: Please upload files using the Upload Attachment button.

comment.desc: Comment or description in a human language
comment.formdesc: Comment or description in a human language.  This will not be correlated with other attributes

target-external.desc: External Target Organizations Affected by this Attack

bic.desc: Bank Identifier Code Number also known as SWIFT-BIC, SWIFT code or ISO 9362 code

bank-account-nr.desc: Bank account number without any routing number

threat-actor.desc: A string identifying the threat actor

vhash.formdesc: You are encouraged to use filename|vhash instead. A checksum from VirusTotal, only use this if you don't know the correct filename

telfhash.desc: telfhash is symbol hash for ELF files, just like imphash is imports hash for PE files.
telfhash.formdesc: You are encouraged to use a file object with telfhash

pehash.desc: peHash - a hash calculated based of certain pieces of a PE executable file

impfuzzy.desc: A fuzzy hash of import table of Portable Executable format

windows-service-name.desc: A windows service name. This is the name used internally by windows. Not to be confused with the windows-service-displayname.

windows-service-displayname.desc: A windows service's displayname, not to be confused with the windows-service-name. This is the name that applications will generally display as the service's name in applications.

whois-registrant-email.desc: The e-mail of a domain's registrant, obtained from the WHOIS information.

whois-registrant-phone.desc: The phone number of a domain's registrant, obtained from the WHOIS information.

whois-registrant-name.desc: The name of a domain's registrant, obtained from the WHOIS information.

whois-registrant-org.desc: The org of a domain's registrant, obtained from the WHOIS information.

whois-registrar.desc: The registrar of the domain, obtained from the WHOIS information.

whois-creation-date.desc: The date of domain's creation, obtained from the WHOIS information.

dns-soa-email.desc: RFC 1035 mandates that DNS zones should have a SOA (Statement Of Authority) record that contains an email address where a PoC for the domain could be contacted. This can sometimes be used for attribution/linkage between different domains even if protected by whois privacy

counter.desc: An integer counter, generally to be used in objects

integer.desc: A generic integer generally to be used in objects

ip-dst|port.desc: IP destination and port number separated by a |

ip-src|port.desc: IP source and port number separated by a |

hostname|port.desc: Hostname and port number separated by a |

email-mime-boundary.desc: The email mime boundary separating parts in a multipart email

first-name.desc: First name of a natural person

middle-name.desc: Middle name of a natural person

last-name.desc: Last name of a natural person

full-name.desc: Full name of a natural person

date-of-birth.desc: Date of birth of a natural person (in YYYY-MM-DD format)

place-of-birth.desc: Place of birth of a natural person

gender.desc: The gender of a natural person (Male, Female, Other, Prefer not to say)

passport-number.desc: The passport number of a natural person

passport-country.desc: The country in which the passport was issued

passport-expiration.desc: The expiration date of a passport

redress-number.desc: The Redress Control Number is the record identifier for people who apply for redress through the DHS Travel Redress Inquiry Program (DHS TRIP). DHS TRIP is for travelers who have been repeatedly identified for additional screening and who want to file an inquiry to have erroneous information corrected in DHS systems

nationality.desc: The nationality of a natural person

issue-date-of-the-visa.desc: The date on which the visa was issued

primary-residence.desc: The primary residence of a natural person

country-of-residence.desc: The country of residence of a natural person

special-service-request.desc: A Special Service Request is a function to an airline to provide a particular facility for A Passenger or passengers.

frequent-flyer-number.desc: The frequent flyer number of a passenger

place-port-of-onward-foreign-destination.desc: A Port where the passenger is transiting to

passenger-name-record-locator-number.desc: The Passenger Name Record Locator is a key under which the reservation for a trip is stored in the system. The PNR contains, among other data, the name, flight segments and address of the passenger. It is defined by a combination of five or six letters and numbers.

mobile-application-id.desc: The application id of a mobile application

boolean.desc: Boolean value - to be used in objects

uuid.desc: UUID - to be used in objects

anonymised.desc: Anonymised value - described with the anonymisation object via a relationship
anonymised.formdesc: Anonymised value - described with the anonymisation object via a relationship.

onion-address.desc: Onion service (formerly known as "hidden service") address

Internal reference.desc: Reference used by the publishing party (e.g. ticket number)

Targeting data.desc: Internal Attack Targeting and Compromise Information
Targeting data.formdesc: Targeting information to include recipient email, infected machines, department, and or locations.

Antivirus detection.desc: All the info about how the malware is detected by the antivirus products
Antivirus detection.formdesc: List of anti-virus vendors detecting the malware or information on detection performance (e.g. 13/43 or 67%). Attachment with list of detection or link to VirusTotal could be placed here as well.

Payload delivery.desc: Information about how the malware is delivered
Payload delivery.formdesc: Information about how the malware payload is initially delivered, for example information about the email or web-site, vulnerability used, originating IP etc. Malware sample itself should be attached here.

Artifacts dropped.desc: Any artifact (files, registry keys etc.) dropped by the malware or other modifications to the system

Payload installation.desc: Info on where the malware gets installed in the system
Payload installation.formdesc: Location where the payload was placed in the system and the way it was installed. For example, a filename|md5 type attribute can be added here like this: c:\windows\system32\malicious.exe|41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e.

Persistence mechanism.desc: Mechanisms used by the malware to start at boot
Persistence mechanism.formdesc: Mechanisms used by the malware to start at boot. This could be a registry key, legitimate driver modification, LNK file in startup

Network activity.desc: Information about network traffic generated by the malware

Payload type.formdesc: Information about the final payload(s). Can contain a function of the payload, e.g. keylogger, RAT, or a name if identified, such as Poison Ivy.

Attribution.desc: Identification of the group, organisation, or country behind the attack

External analysis.desc: Any other result from additional analysis of the malware like tools output
External analysis.formdesc: Any other result from additional analysis of the malware like tools output Examples: pdf-parser output, automated sandbox analysis, reverse engineering report.

Financial fraud.formdesc: Financial Fraud indicators, for example: IBAN Numbers, BIC codes, Credit card numbers, etc.

Support Tool.desc: Tools supporting analysis or detection of the event

Other.desc: Attributes that are not part of any other category or are meant to be used as a component in MISP objects
